summary: Refined architectural governance by integrating advanced numerical methods, including AST-parsing, Bayesian anomaly detection, and manifold learning, to optimize development cycles and system reliability. Key implementations include a decorator-based Gaussian Latency Monitor (GLM) and the use of PCA-preprocessed UMAP/t-SNE for semantic visualization, shifting focus from task-based metrics to structural rationale and uncertainty modeling.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and Pydantic validation ensure system determinism.
Bayesian inference, KL divergence, and Gaussian models (Poisson/Beta) are essential for modeling uncertainty and anomaly detection.
Numerical stability requires condition number monitoring and epsilon-guarded normalization.
UMAP and t-SNE, with PCA preprocessing, effectively visualize semantic stagnation and thematic drift.
Implementing a 'burn-in' period is critical for rolling statistics to avoid false positives.
Architectural documentation is most valuable when it captures the rationale behind implementation choices.

summary: Enhanced architectural telemetry and benchmarking rigor by implementing a 'stats_engine.py' module. This transition shifted focus from general orchestration to robust statistical validation, utilizing hypothesis testing, distribution checks, and bootstrap resampling to ensure P99 latency metrics are reliable and free from noise-induced misinterpretation.
key_learnings: Statistical significance requires evaluating effect size alongside p-values to avoid misinterpreting noise.
Automated testing suites must include distribution checks (e.g., Shapiro-Wilk) to validate parametric tests.
Minimum sample size thresholds are critical safeguards against p-hacking.
Point estimates are insufficient; bootstrap resampling provides necessary confidence intervals for tail-latency metrics.
Computational efficiency in bootstrapping is maintained via m-out-of-n subsampling.
